subtopicTitle: Sign convention for mirrors and lenses

cards.front: In the New Cartesian Sign Convention, where is the origin placed, and what does the principal axis represent?
cards.back: The origin is placed at the pole (P) for mirrors or the optical centre (O) for lenses. The principal axis is taken as the X-axis.

cards.front: According to the New Cartesian Sign Convention, how are distances measured along the principal axis assigned positive or negative signs?
cards.back: All distances measured from the pole/optical centre in the direction of incident light are taken as positive. Distances measured opposite to the direction of incident light are taken as negative.

cards.front: How are heights of objects and images assigned signs in the New Cartesian Sign Convention?
cards.back: Heights measured upwards and perpendicular to the principal axis (above the X-axis) are taken as positive. Heights measured downwards and perpendicular to the principal axis (below the X-axis) are taken as negative.

cards.front: For a real object placed to the left of a mirror or lens, with light incident from the left, what is the sign of the object distance, $u$, according to the New Cartesian Sign Convention?
cards.back: The object distance, $u$, is negative. This is because the object is placed to the left of the pole/optical centre, meaning its distance is measured opposite to the direction of incident light.

cards.front: What are the signs of the focal length, $f$, for a concave mirror and a convex lens, and why, under the New Cartesian Sign Convention (light from left)?
cards.back:
• Concave Mirror: $f < 0$. Its real focus is in front of the mirror (left of pole), so its distance is measured opposite to incident light.
  • Convex Lens: $f > 0$. Its real focus is on the opposite side of the lens (right of optical centre), so its distance is measured in the direction of incident light.

cards.front: What are the signs of the focal length, $f$, for a convex mirror and a concave lens, and why, under the New Cartesian Sign Convention (light from left)?
cards.back:
• Convex Mirror: $f > 0$. Its virtual focus is behind the mirror (right of pole), so its distance is measured in the direction of incident light.
  • Concave Lens: $f < 0$. Its virtual focus is in front of the lens (left of optical centre), so its distance is measured opposite to incident light.

cards.front: Using the New Cartesian Sign Convention (light from left), what is the sign of the image distance, $v$, for: 1. A real image by a mirror? 2. A real image by a lens? 3. A virtual image by a mirror? 4. A virtual image by a lens?
cards.back:
• 1. Real image by mirror: $v < 0$. Real images are formed in front of the mirror (left), opposite to incident light.
  • 2. Real image by lens: $v > 0$. Real images are formed behind the lens (right), in the direction of incident light.
  • 3. Virtual image by mirror: $v > 0$. Virtual images are formed behind the mirror (right), in the direction of incident light.
  • 4. Virtual image by lens: $v < 0$. Virtual images are formed in front of the lens (left), opposite to incident light.

cards.front: In the context of the New Cartesian Sign Convention, what does a positive value for magnification ($M$) indicate about the image, and what does a negative $M$ indicate?
cards.back:
• A positive magnification ($M > 0$) indicates that the image is erect (upright) and has the same orientation as the object. This typically corresponds to a virtual image.
  • A negative magnification ($M < 0$) indicates that the image is inverted (upside-down) relative to the object. This typically corresponds to a real image.
